subject: SIG follow-up: Architecture diagrams, IAM screenshots, and attestation checklist
messages:
From: Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Robert Chen <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: SIG follow-up: architecture & IAM evidence

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for completing the initial SIG questionnaire yesterday. Our security team has a couple of follow-ups before we can move to procurement: specifically, we need a short network architecture diagram that highlights traffic flow between the control plane and private workloads, and screenshots showing IAM roles/policies for service accounts used by Redwood Private.

If possible could you: 
- Share a Drive folder with the diagram (PDF or PNG) and the IAM screenshots (high level, redacted tokens).
- Confirm where audit logs are stored and retention period for access logs.
- Provide a signed attestation or simple statement that the policies in the SIG responses are currently in effect.

We'd appreciate these by EOD Thursday (13 Aug) to keep our procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
Security Manager, Acme Corp

[External Sender]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Robert Chen <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: architecture & IAM evidence

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Marcus and Mina from Security Ops and Compliance. Quick plan: 

1) I'll upload a concise network architecture diagram and an access-control slide that calls out VPC peering, ingress filters, and control-plane endpoints.
2) Mina will pull IAM screenshots for the Redwood Private deployment role and redact sensitive IDs.
3) Marcus will confirm audit log locations and retention and provide the attestation text.

Upload ETA: later today for the diagram and tomorrow morning for screenshots + attestation.

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[jordan_blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134]
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>, Robert Chen <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: architecture & IAM evidence

Jordan / Elena —

Uploaded the requested artifacts to Drive: short list below, folder shared with Elena
- drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-redwood-sig-evidence (shared view-only)
  - architecture-diagram-private-controlplane-20260811.png (diagram, highlights control plane endpoints and VPC boundaries)
  - iam-service-role-screenshots-20260811.zip (collection of redacted screenshots; see README inside)
  - sig-attestation-acme-answers-20260811.pdf (signed attestation by Redwood Compliance)

Quick notes: 
- Audit logs: control plane and deployment audit events are stored in our central logging account (GCS) with a default retention of 540 days. Access logs for the Private runtime are retained for 365 days.
- The IAM screenshots include role names and policy statements; we redacted principals and account IDs as requested. README includes the redaction mapping and how to verify signatures locally.

Flag for procurement: the attestation is a short statement confirming that the policies described in the SIG responses are active as of 2026-08-11. If legal requires additional language we can adjust and re-sign.

[Mina Haddad
Security Operations, Redwood Inference]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: architecture & IAM evidence

Elena —

Confirming a couple of items inline: 
- Audit log storage: GCS bucket: gs://redwood-controlplane-logs (read-only view links provided to Acme in the Drive folder). Retention: 540 days for control-plane, 365 days for runtime access logs.
- Access to logs: we can provide temporary IAM-granted view-only access via a support ticket if your team needs to inspect specific events.
- Attestation: signed PDF is in the folder; text begins: "Redwood Inference attests that the administrative and access control policies described in the attached SIG responses are in effect as of 2026-08-11." Let us know any edits.

Attachment stubs: [attachment: sig-attestation-acme-answers-20260811.pdf (application/pdf)]

If the procurement team needs a short walkthrough call to validate the artifacts, I can join Thursday 10:00am PT.

—Marcus
Director, Platform Security, Redwood Inference
From: Elena Torres <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Robert Chen <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 11:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: architecture & IAM evidence

Team —

Received everything, thank you. I spot-checked the diagram and the README in the IAM bundle. Two quick asks before we close the audit: 
1) Can you add one slide to the diagram PDF that documents the encryption-at-rest keys and where KMS is managed (customer-managed vs Redwood-managed)?
2) Please include the exact retention policy bullet for access logs in the attestation PDF (just the one line stating retention durations).

If you can drop those two small updates before EOD Friday we can move the procurement packet to legal review. Would also like to schedule a 20-minute walkthrough on Friday at 9:30am PT to review access-scope assumptions — Jordan, could you set up the invite?

Thanks again — this was quick and helpful.

Elena Torres
Security Manager, Acme Corp
